qs.q: A 6-year-old child presents with fatigue and intermittent jaundice. Laboratory results show a mean corpuscular hemoglobin concentration (MCHC) of 36 g/dL and a red cell distribution width (RDW) of 13%. Which diagnosis is most consistent with these findings?
qs.e: An MCHC greater than 35 g/dL combined with an RDW less than 14% is a suggested screening test for hereditary spherocytosis. Iron deficiency and thalassemia typically present with low MCHC, not elevated.

qs.q: A patient with sickle cell anemia experiences intracellular dehydration and increased mean corpuscular hemoglobin concentration (MCHC). What is the direct consequence of this change on the pathophysiology?
qs.e: Intracellular dehydration leads to an increased MCHC, which strongly promotes HbS polymerization and increases sickling. Decreased oxygen affinity or pH also promotes sickling, but MCHC is directly tied to cell concentration.
